subject: Clarify data residency and default deletion for derived artifacts (prompts, outputs)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finbridge.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify retention for prompts vs derived outputs

Hi Soojin,

Quick follow-up from our security intake — we need a concise answer for two items before the procurement call next week:

1) Are user-submitted prompts treated as stored customer data by default? If so, do they count toward the retention TTL or are they considered ephemeral and purged more quickly?

2) How are model-generated artifacts (summaries, embeddings, reranked results) classified for residency and deletion? Specifically: are those kept on the default hosted stack and for how long, and can we opt to never store certain derived outputs?

We already scanned your public docs but would appreciate one definitive statement we can share with our legal and infra teams. Attaching a screenshot of the section that confused us.

Thanks,
Liam
Security Engineering
FinBridge

Attachment: screenshot-question.png

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify retention for prompts vs derived outputs

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear questions and the screenshot. High-level answers:

- Prompts (raw user input) are captured by default on the hosted API for a limited default horizon to support debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring. They are not indefinitely archived unless a customer enables longer retention or exports.

- Model-generated artifacts (summaries, embeddings, reranks) are considered "derived artifacts." By default these are retained for a different, configurable horizon than raw requests; we treat many derivatives as persistent artifacts because they can be used for features like embedding indexes or reranking caches.

However, to avoid any ambiguity when you brief legal/infra I want to confirm the exact default TTLs and options for opt-out/never-store. Looping in Marissa (policy) and Karthik (product infra) to provide the canonical TTLs and the erasure evidence path.

On it — will consolidate into a single short summary for your team.

— Soojin
Senior Security Partner, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

On Sat, Jul 18, 2026 at 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Liam — thanks for the clear questions...

Adding the canonical policy language (short):

- Default capture behavior: Hosted API captures requests and final responses (request/response pairs) for 45 days by default for debugging and quality. Streaming token buffers used during active sessions are ephemeral and not persisted beyond the session unless the final response is recorded.

- Prompt classification: "Prompt" (what the user sends) is recorded as a request artifact. If a customer opts into "do not store prompts," we offer an account-level opt-out that prevents storing raw request bodies and removes them from short-term logs; derived artifacts that were already generated must be handled via erasure (see below).

- Derived artifacts (summaries, completions, embeddings): Treated as "derived results." The default TTL for derived results is 90 days on hosted plans because they are frequently relied upon by built-in features (caching, embeddings indexes). Customers may configure retention policies per project: shorter TTLs (e.g., 0 days) are supported, and Dedicated/Private deployments can enforce on-prem rules.

- Erasure path & evidence: We provide an API and compliance runbook for selective erasure requests. Once a deletion job completes we emit a deletion report (job id + object list + timestamps) and can provide proof-of-deletion artifacts for compliance reviews. For enterprise plans we also support exportable deletion logs and optionally a signed attestation.

I attached a concise summary PDF and a short erasure-playbook text excerpt you can share with FinBridge. Karthik — flag if any infra nuance needs changing.

— Marissa
Director, Product Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retention-summary-v2.pdf, example-erasure-playbook.txt

Subject: Re: Clarify retention for prompts vs derived outputs

Hi Liam — consolidated answer below (feel free to copy-paste into your intake):

1) Prompts (user-supplied inputs)
- Default: Stored as request artifacts for 45 days on hosted accounts for debugging/abuse detection.
- Opt-out: Account-level "do not store prompts" available; enabling prevents future prompt capture. Previously captured prompts are removed via a deletion job (see erasure path).

2) Derived artifacts (model outputs, embeddings, reranks, summaries)
- Default: Classified as "derived results" with a 90-day default retention on hosted plans. These are retained because they power features like caching and embedding-based search.
- Opt-out/configuration: You may set a project-level retention TTL (including immediate purge). Dedicated/Private customers can enforce their own residency/TTL.

3) Streaming tokens / session buffers
- Transient only during an active session. We do not persist intermediate streaming buffers by default; only the final response is stored according to the retention rules above.

4) Deletion & evidence
- We support selective erasure via the Compliance Erasure API. After a deletion job completes you receive a deletion report (job id + timestamp). For enterprise customers we can also provide an attestation or a signed proof-of-deletion for audits.

Attached: redwood-retention-summary-v2.pdf (one-page summary) and example-erasure-playbook.txt (how to request erasure + expected timelines). Also linking our shared QnA doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2bRetentionQnA.

If your legal team wants formal contract language we can provide a short addendum describing the retention defaults and the opt-out mechanism — happy to loop in our legal team next week.
